text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.4% today as oil markets reacted to escalating geopolitical tension in the Middle East. Iran's threats of retaliation for U.S. strikes, combined with actual attacks on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz this week, pushed crude prices sharply higher—Brent touched $110 a barrel Friday, and the gap between U.S. crude ($101.91) and world oil ($126.55) has widened dramatically. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly lift earnings from production and refining operations.

The stock's 15.6% gain over two weeks reflects a broader flight to safety as Middle East disruption threatens global oil supply. Even Trump's statement ruling out nuclear weapons and ground troops didn't ease the rally; instead, the market is pricing in the real risk of sustained shipping delays and refinery disruptions—which makes crude scarcer and more expensive, benefiting producers with established reserves and infrastructure.
